# PathSharer Backend — LLM Reference (`llms.txt`)

> This file follows the [llmstxt.org](https://llmstxt.org) convention.
> For the full agent guide, see [AGENTS.md](./AGENTS.md).

## Service Summary

**PathSharer Backend** is the Node.js + Express + Socket.IO server for the PathSharer platform.  
It provides REST APIs for guest auth, active-user registration, co-passenger proximity search,
1-on-1 chat history and image uploads, journey management, and push notifications.
It also maintains persistent WebSocket connections for real-time chat, ride-connect requests,
and online-presence tracking.

- Port: 5000 (default)
- API prefix: `/api/v1`
- Health check: `GET /health`

## Tech Stack

Node.js + TypeScript · Express v5 · Socket.IO v4 · MongoDB + Mongoose v9 · Redis v5 · JWT · Expo Server SDK (push) · Multer · Zod · Helmet · express-rate-limit

## Source Layout

```
src/
  server.ts               ← entry point (DB, Redis, HTTP, Socket.IO)
  app.ts                  ← Express setup: middleware + routes + error handler
  config/env.ts           ← typed env config
  database/
    connection.ts         ← Mongoose helpers
    redis.ts              ← Redis client helpers
  middlewares/
    auth.middleware.ts    ← JWT verify → req.userId
    error.middleware.ts   ← central error handler
    logger.middleware.ts  ← request logger
  models/
    user.model.ts         ← IUser (name, phone, gender, expoPushToken, recentSearches)
    activeUser.model.ts   ← IActiveUser (userId, source, dest, isActive) — Redis-backed
    message.model.ts      ← IMessage (sender, receiver, type, content, imageUrl, read)
    journey.model.ts      ← IJourney
    userJourney.model.ts  ← IUserJourney
    notification.model.ts ← INotification
  routes/                 ← one file per resource, mounted in routes/index.ts
  controllers/            ← one file per resource
  services/
    findCoPassenger.service.ts  ← Redis-first nearby search, Mongo fallback
    push-notification.service.ts← Expo push (sendRingNotification)
    matching.service.ts         ← route-overlap algorithm
    booking.service.ts          ← booking + fare
    pricing.service.ts          ← per-km fare
    auth.service.ts             ← generateJWT
  sockets/
    index.ts              ← initSocketIO, JWT auth middleware, room wiring
    events.ts             ← SOCKET_EVENTS enum + payload interfaces
    chat.socket.ts        ← send_message, typing, read, online tracking
    ride.socket.ts        ← connect_request, connect_response
    journey.socket.ts     ← journey room join/leave
    notification.socket.ts← notification events
  utils/
    upload.ts             ← Multer disk config
    name-generator.ts     ← random animal names for guests
  validators/
    activeUser.validator.ts ← Zod schema
```

## Key API Endpoints

```
POST   /api/v1/auth/web-guest              # auto-create guest (no auth)
POST   /api/v1/active-users                # register as searching (auth)
GET    /api/v1/active-users/nearby         # ?srcLng=&srcLat=&dstLng=&dstLat= (auth)
DELETE /api/v1/active-users/me             # deregister (auth)
GET    /api/v1/messages/conversations      # conversation list (auth)
GET    /api/v1/messages/:otherUserId       # paginated history (auth)
POST   /api/v1/messages/upload-image       # multipart image upload (auth)
GET    /api/v1/users/me/recent-searches    # (auth)
POST   /api/v1/users/me/recent-searches    # (auth)
GET    /api/v1/config                      # public app metadata
GET    /health                             # { status, db, redis }
```

## Key Socket.IO Events

Client → Server: `chat:send_message`, `chat:typing`, `chat:read`,
`ride:connect_request`, `ride:connect_response`, `journey:join_room`, `journey:leave_room`

Server → Client: `chat:message`, `chat:message_read`, `chat:online_status`,
`ride:connect_request_incoming`, `ride:connect_response_result`,
`notification:new`, `notification:ring`, `error`

## Key Facts for AI Agents

- All Socket.IO connections authenticate via `{ auth: { token } }` in handshake.
- Personal socket room name: `"user:{userId}"` — always emit to rooms, never socket IDs.
- Redis key `active-user:{userId}` expires in 3600 s (1 hour); Redis is a soft dependency.
- Guest phone placeholder pattern: `/^0{9}\d+$/` — do not change this regex.
- Uploaded images stored in `../uploads/`, served at `/uploads/*`.
- Guest user names are random (adjective + animal) and regenerate on each search.
- CORS is `*` in dev, locked to same-origin in production.
